A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Argus study and include the complete four-page supplementary material. Corresponding text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, baseline comparisons in Tables 1–2, ablations in Table 3, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative experiments, ablations and qualitative results, including the supplementary comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same diffusion model, training objective, camera-motion simulation, view-based alignment, blended decoding and context-conditioned long-video generation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated 360-1M training data and evaluation coverage: panoramic generation, geometric consistency, in-the-wild videos, stabilization, viewpoint control and interactive VQA.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain PanoDiffusion, Be-Your-Outpainter and Follow-Your-Canvas. The stabilization reference in Figure 8 and SVD/COSMOS comparisons in supplementary Figure 17 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Training stages, resolutions, budgets, evaluation metrics and ground-truth camera-pose controls remain unchanged. Both versions report the same 101-video evaluation, 15-video line-consistency set and 48-smartphone-video geometry analysis.

E4.justification: Table 3 and Figure 6 retain the same alignment and decoding ablations and VAE reconstruction reference. Scene-dynamics, geometric-plausibility and supplementary failure-case analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. No statistical uncertainty reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains Argus PSNR values of 21.83 and 21.50 for real and simulated camera trajectories, respectively. Supplementary result images also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of Equations 1–12, including the loss, motion simulation, blending and supplementary projection derivation, is unchanged. Minor spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about coherent video-to-360 generation, geometry- and motion-aware components, generalization and downstream applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations of alignment, boundary consistency and scene dynamics are unchanged. Both versions retain the resolution and physical-consistency limitations and the qualification that generated views may not provide factual grounding for VQA.

D1.justification: Supplementary Sections 2–3 retain the same filtering procedures, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, inference instructions and baseline implementations. Project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 62 references and related-work discussion remain, including positioning relative to VidPanos, Imagine360 and 360DVD. No cited work or substantive positioning statement is added or removed.

P1.justification: The marginal identifier changes from v1, dated 10 April 2025, to v3, dated 23 April 2026. Main and supplementary wording, headings and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and three tables retain their content, captions and placement. Differences are limited to small typesetting shifts, the marginal version stamp and the embedded-animation display implementation; animation image content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Both versions contain the same scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility details and limitations, including the supplement. The minor editorial and PDF presentation changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's clarity or evidential strength.
